body: @cwilso Can you please add me to the invite list for the meeting tomorrow when you get a chance, thanks!
@monica-ch yes, but you need to send me your email address (to cwilso@google.com)

We have a carryover about https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/10432 from last week, but unfortunately I cannot join this week. I will bring it up again in at a future meeting.

**EDIT:** Maybe I will be able to join in the second half.

Minutes from 02/12:

- **Controls for Image Element** Noam Rosenthal introduced the carryover item regarding controls for the image element. Yoel Hawa explained the controls attribute is proposed to mirror video controls, providing interactive UI for images, particularly driven by needs for spatial media and related to animated images. Lea Verou noted this would be very useful for animated images and inquired how this new attribute would interact with the CSS image animation property.
- **Discussion on Controls Attribute Design** Keith Cirkel raised concerns about repeating the "all or nothing" mistake of video controls and suggested making controls a DOM token list for finer grain control, though they noted the WebKit team has expressed an objection towards overly prescriptive controls. Keith Cirkel also encouraged developing this in tandem with media elements (audio and video) to generalize the approach. Anne van Kesteren emphasized that a simple first step is to achieve parity with audio and video by adding the basic controls attribute to image elements, which they do not classify as a failure for media elements.
- **Concerns about Detailed Control and Privacy** Anne van Kesteren explained that concerns have been raised by the WebKit media team regarding giving detailed control over controls, specifically the ability to suppress controls like full screen, and the potential privacy and fingerprinting factor of providing a readback of available controls. Noam Rosenthal was supportive of exploring a middle ground for customizability and avoiding embedding animated GIFs within video tags. Keith Cirkel questioned what a blanket controls attribute would mean for static images versus animated images or SVGs.
- **Usability Cliff and Customization** Lea Verou agreed that controls is a good first step, but highlighted the "usability cliff" where authors must reimplement the entire toolbar to add a single button. Lea Verou suggested that allowing authors to opt in and out of certain controls has value, as it enables user agents to add new functionality without the burden of it always being present. Stephen Chenney and Luke stressed the importance of defining how the proposed HTML attribute would mediate with the new CSS image animation property to avoid conflicts.
- **Status of Image Animation Property and Path Forward** Lea Verou confirmed the CSS image animation draft was accepted in January, with user control being an explicit goal. Stephen Chenney indicated that the CSS spec is at a stage where it could be worked off of. Anne van Kesteren requested implementer interest for the minimal version of the proposal and suggested that any animation control implemented for images should tie into the CSS property. Noam Rosenthal agreed to internally inquire about Chromium's opinion.
- **Coordinates of Keyboard Driven Click** Anne van Kesteren presented the issue of keyboard-driven clicks sometimes resulting in 0,0 coordinates, while WebKit uses the element's midpoint for privacy and accessibility reasons. Anne van Kesteren noted that Apple's accessibility people consider the midpoint behavior a requirement for assistive technology and suggested keeping the behavior consistent for all keyboard users. Mason Freed requested clarification on what specific issues arise for accessibility if 0,0 is used. Olli Pettay mentioned that their accessibility features return the middle point when clicking, but for keyboard use, it remains 0,0, and also pointed out a discrepancy in scrolling behavior when focusing elements before pressing enter. The action item is to seek feedback from accessibility experts.
- **Form Control Range Interface (Opaque Range)** Stephanie Zhang presented the opaque range proposal (formerly form control range), which aims to provide geometry for a subrange of text within form elements like input or textarea to facilitate things like tooltips or custom highlighting. The design involves a new abstract range subtype that keeps internal DOM hidden while providing geometry methods and being a live range. Stephanie Zhang requested moving to stage two, noting implementation has begun in Edge.
- **Discussion on Opaque Range Implementation and Stage Two Approval** Anne van Kesteren confirmed the internal model now uses a hidden container node and offset, which aligns with the desired general shape. Olli Pettay pointed out the need for an API to remove these effectively live ranges, suggesting a disconnect method on the range itself. Anne van Kesteren and Stephanie Zhang agreed with the need for a disconnect method. The group approved moving the proposal to stage two.
- **Canvas Writing Mode** Stephen Chenney requested feedback and standards positions on a spec PR adding writing mode and text orientation support for canvas text. They highlighted alignment issues, specifically with how baselines are defined for vertical text, as the primary challenge in drawing the text. Someone in Monsters University (Hybrid Meeting Room) (us-cam-5cc) noted that the central baseline is typically used for vertical text.
- b Jayson Chen from Microsoft Edge introduced the problem that the select element does not support slotted options, which is an issue for custom select elements. Lea Verou and Mason Freed strongly agreed that this is a broken behavior that should be fixed, and Mason Freed suggested focusing on fixing it for the newer customizable select first, though fixing both new and old selects is the ultimate goal. Luke and Keith Cirkel insisted on fixing it for all selects consistently, including taking a serious look at datalist. Olli Pettay cautioned that fixing this may not be trivial and requires tweaking several algorithms. The group agreed to move the proposal to stage one.
- **Platform Provided Behavior for Custom Elements** Ana Sollano Kim presented a proposal for "platform provided behaviors" to address custom element authors' requests, starting with a submit behavior to allow custom buttons to submit forms implicitly, participate in accessibility, and manage pseudo classes. The framework is designed to be scalable to other behaviors like label and radio buttons. Keith Cirkel liked the idea of composable objects but wanted a rough sketch of how this would extend to userland behaviors and suggested using a more opaque structure than an array for the behaviors list.
- **Debate on Low-Level Capabilities vs. Abstraction** Lea Verou argued that the proposal might be "putting the cart before the horse" by packaging behaviors before exposing low-level capabilities individually, suggesting that common needs like focusability should be solved generically first. Lea Verou expressed concern that the current proposal might be misused if authors cannot access the low-level behaviors in any other way. Mason Freed and Luke supported the current level of abstraction as it addresses a core use case without exposing developers to a "bag of foot guns" and agreed that solving focusability is important but not a prerequisite.
- **Concerns with API Shape and Completeness** Luke and Mason Freed noted that the current approach is similar to how command invokers were handled by adding behaviors incrementally and thinking about conflicts. Luke questioned how conflicting behaviors in an array would be resolved and suggested the API shape should prevent such contradictions. Lea Verou observed that the list of button behaviors in the explainer seems incomplete (e.g., missing popover and command target) and worried about the implications of adding new behaviors to a "black box" in the future. Mason Freed defended the black box approach, noting that it aligns with how new features are added to existing elements like the native button.
- **Explainer Updates and Future Discussions** Ana Sollano Kim announced they will update the explainer with a more concise proposal regarding conflicts and resolution, and will also include examples of composability to better prepare for further exploration of the topic. Noam Rosenthal mentioned they had to drop, and Mason Freed suggested picking up the main discussion at the next meeting, while Keith Cirkel allowed Ana Sollano Kim to provide their closing comments.
- **Challenges with Element Internals and API Surface** Lea Verou and Luke discussed the idea of command invoker behavior, noting that configuring it would still be necessary even with a button mixing. Lea Verou expressed concern that the current approach using elementInternals is problematic because it cannot add API surface like real mixins or traits, requiring extensive glue code for wiring up attributes and getters/setters for features like command and command for. Lea Verou pointed out that solving low-level issues might allow browser-provided traits to become available through work in TC39, which could provide necessary API surface.
- **Prioritizing Unsolvable Problems and Focusability** Lea Verou argued that the most pressing pain points are issues that currently cannot be solved, such as focusability and CSS pseudo-classes, suggesting that solving impossible things is more crucial than improving the ergonomics of things that are already possible. Lea Verou emphasized that custom elements should ideally behave as closely as possible to native form elements to extend familiar concepts. Luke and Lea Verou agreed that focusability should be prioritized, with Luke suggesting a simple implementation similar to tabindex zero as a starting point, which could be made more granular later.
- **The Role of Behavior Bundles and Accessibility** Luke stated that behavior bundles are important because combining behaviors, such as button activation and focusability, helps prevent misuse and ensures accessibility, which Lea Verou agreed with. Lea Verou further clarified that features making sense outside of buttons should not be restricted to the button bundle, even though they support making button activation conditional on focusability. Luke stressed that focusability should be the first step in addressing these issues.
- **Need for a Comprehensive List of Behaviors** Luke and Lea Verou discussed the lack of a complete list of behaviors that custom elements cannot currently access, such as labelable, popover target, and command invoker target, calling it important research work. They questioned why the discussion frequently centers on button submit, suggesting there might be a specific pressing need at Microsoft. Luke requested a list of all potential atomic behaviors that could constitute these bundles.
- **Labelability and Form Association** Lea Verou and Luke addressed the issue of labelability, noting that elements like <meter> and <progress> are labelable but not form associated. Luke has an open issue to allow custom elements to be labelable without being form associated to replicate this behavior. They concluded that form associated is somewhat of a bundle, as not everything labelable is a form element, and Lea Verou criticized the current implementation of form associated and element internals for not providing standard platform properties for free.
- **The Language Barrier: Traits and Protocols** Lea Verou explained their involvement in first-class protocols in TC39, viewing it as a solution for the challenges related to web components needing traits in the language. Lea Verou mentioned working with Michael and Jordan Art to resurrect an abandoned Stage 1 proposal for traits, with progress expected to be presented at the March meeting. Luke acknowledged that the main difficulty with TC39 is achieving consensus on the shape of the proposal rather than the technical implementation.


Minutes from 02-19:

Minutes
- Discussed OOO HTML streaming, current direction is to keep start/end marker until template element popped.
- Important to keep the parent element as context and insertion point in that element
- Defer commit
- Worry about differences in impl (e.g. bfcache) leaves pages in a broken state in some browsers.
- Possible to design the API to make it clearer where to restore (e.g. two callbacks in one method)
- Farre: would prefer to wait with introducing new changes to session history, navigation, and navigation api, until current issues are resolved and we’re in a better state for Interop 2026.
